slides.title: Introduction to Function Templates
slides.prompt: Function templates allow you to write a single generic function that works with multiple data types. The compiler automatically deduces template arguments based on the function parameters passed during invocation.

slides.title: Template Parameter Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in the missing keyword used to declare a generic type parameter inside template brackets.

slides.title: Explicit Template Arguments
slides.prompt: What happens when you call myMax<double>(10, 20.5) with explicit template arguments?
options: The template argument T is forced to double, converting the integer 10 to 10.0
A compilation error occurs due to argument mismatch
The compiler ignores the explicit template argument and deduces T as int
slides.correctAnswer: The template argument T is forced to double, converting the integer 10 to 10.0

slides.title: Multiple Template Parameters
slides.prompt: Fill in the template declaration header to support two distinct generic types for function arguments.

slides.title: Type Deduction Failure
slides.prompt: Given template <typename T> T add(T a, T b), what occurs if you invoke add(5, 3.14)?
options: Compilation error because T cannot be deduced consistently as both int and double
Implicit conversion occurs automatically converting 3.14 to int
Implicit conversion occurs automatically converting 5 to double
The compiler creates two separate template functions
slides.correctAnswer: Compilation error because T cannot be deduced consistently as both int and double

slides.title: Template Function Overloading
slides.prompt: Fill in the non-template function call syntax to explicitly prefer calling a standard overload over a template function when names match.

slides.title: Template Instantiation Timing
slides.prompt: When is the actual machine code for a specific function template instantiation generated by C++?
options: At compile time when the template is invoked with specific concrete arguments
At runtime when the function call statement is executed
At link time by the dynamic linker
slides.correctAnswer: At compile time when the template is invoked with specific concrete arguments

slides.title: Trailing Return Type with decltype
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used in C++11 trailing return type syntax for function templates.

slides.title: Keyword Equivalence in Template Header
slides.prompt: In template declarations, what is the difference between template <typename T> and template <class T>?
options: There is no functional difference; both keywords are completely interchangeable in type parameters
typename allows primitive types while class requires a user-defined struct/class type
class requires the argument to inherit from a base class
typename can only be used with C++20 concepts
slides.correctAnswer: There is no functional difference; both keywords are completely interchangeable in type parameters

slides.title: Abbreviated Function Templates (C++20)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword introduced in C++20 to simplify function template syntax directly in parameter lists.
